verdicts.reason: Quotes verified verbatim. realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:122 D-05 does read 'Overdub also runs on the locked stack and carries the provenance intact', header :5-6 is '[BREADTH] / Last updated: 2026-07-16', while realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:5-6 is '[DEEP] / Last updated: 2026-07-18' with CX-07 at :138-150 stating overdub yields delivery-certainty at grade `delivered-by`. 08.07-overdub-mode.md:16-17 names the defect explicitly ('the domain index's D-05 carries the uncorrected claim') and :333 routes it to Step 6, which has since produced the CX without editing the index. That is a genuine un-remediated stale assertion in the domain key file with no marker on it. DOWNGRADED to warning on two grounds: (a) the finding's second half is wrong — index:121 D-04 ('ships with any session mechanism, including Overdub') is NOT contradicted; CX-07 :149 confirms overdub does write an attendance row, merely at a lower grade; (b) nothing is uninventable — the graded semantics are fully specified in 08.07 D-04 (:353), CX-07 (:140-150) and 08.05.04:50/:166, so an implementer cannot be forced to invent product behaviour, only to notice the index rationale is stale.

Quotes verified (08.07-overdub-mode.md:248, :250, :251, :291), but no implementer diverges. 08.07:251 is normative and unhedged ('Accepted and aligned. 08 does not enforce commercial deadlines'), it is restated as a locked decision at :356 D-07 ('08 never enforces a commercial deadline — it records timestamps and 05 decides what late costs. A platform that bins a late take has destroyed work'), and the same posture is applied again at :263 for a cancelled request ('Passes may still be delivered against the closed request and are preserved as evidence'). Against three convergent normative statements, ':248 persists until the request expires' is a retention gloss, not a competing rule — and :291's Expired trigger is 'Deadline passed, nothing delivered', which by its own wording does not describe an in-flight upload. The missing Expired-exit transition is state-machine completeness, which belongs to the IA layer, not to vision.

All three loci verified. 08.07-overdub-mode.md:172-176 presents a three-row table headed 'Grade' whose third row is 'Counter-attested', and D-04 at :353 repeats 'The record states its own basis (`delivered-by` / `observed-playing` / `counter-attested`)'. The owning record 08.05.04-session-attendance-provenance.md:50 gives the grade field exactly two values and models attestation as a separate orthogonal axis with its own states (:178 'Unattested', :179 'Self-attested') and its own decision D-11 (:234) — never as a grade rung. realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:225 writes the ladder as '`delivered-by` < `observed-playing` < `session-captured+attested`', a third identifier which 08.05.04:207 attributes to domain 02's candidate ladder rather than to 08's own field. So whether counter-attestation is a value of the exported grade or a separate axis is genuinely unsettled across the three files that define, own and export it. DOWNGRADED to warning: the enum's literal identifiers are a data-model naming call for /create-prd-architecture, and both readings produce the same observable product behaviour (acceptance is recorded and visible either way).

Quotes verified (realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:82; 08.05.02-take-alignment-drift-correction.md:76-79, :261, :298), but the owning feature does not merely disagree with the CX — it names and corrects that exact CX wording in-line. 08.05.02:261 DT-04 says '"just correlate the tracks" — the obvious first idea, and what the parent CX's "degrade to correlation" implies — cannot work on raw tracks', and :264 DT-07 records that it 'sharpens the domain CX (line 105: "if the reference is absent, alignment degrades to correlation rather than failing")'. A reader is therefore explicitly told the CX phrasing is loose. The buildable rule lives entirely in 08.05.02 (the R1-R4 ladder at :71-74, D-01 :294, D-05 :298), and the CX bullet carries no implementable detail; it is a synthesis note, not a competing specification.

Quotes verified (08.07-overdub-mode.md:327, :312; moscow-ledger.md:558 places 08.01.01 at COULD, :565 places 08.06 at COULD, :83 places 08.07 at MUST), but nothing is left to invent. 08.07 owns and mandates the two capabilities itself: D-05 at :354 ('The player's local round-trip is measured per rig, per session — never assumed — and is the offset alignment uses') and Happy Path steps 5-6 (:222-223). Those are 08.07's own decisions, so they ship inside the 08.07 slice regardless of how 08.01.01/08.06 are tiered — a MoSCoW tier ranks a feature node, it does not delete a dependency a MUST feature restates as its own decision. The ledger row for 08.01.01 (:558) also says something narrower than the finding claims: 'Its residual value if the rooms are cut is routing people into Overdub — which does not require a measurement to do' addresses routing, not the local round-trip calibration 08.07 D-05 specifies, so the two texts are not in contradiction.

Quote verified at 08.07-overdub-mode.md:267, and the request model at :218 does indeed declare no size/duration bound. But the product behaviour on that same row is fully stated and requires no bound to implement: 'Accepted if it is genuinely a long multichannel pass', with the User Sees column reading 'Progress, and a size warning against their own remaining upload, not a refusal'. Nothing is rejected, so no acceptance threshold is a vision-layer decision — an upload ceiling is a storage/quota value owned by /create-prd-architecture. The clause 'Bounded by the request's declared scope, not by a guess' is a prohibition on inventing an arbitrary cap, which is the opposite of forcing one.

Verified on disk and internally self-contradictory within one file. realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:52-53 reads '5 sub-domains, 3 domain-level features, 20 leaf features. All `[SURFACE]` — breadth pass only; depth is allocated by MoSCoW in `/ideate-discover` Step 5', while the table immediately beneath it marks 08.01-08.05 `[BREADTH]` (:57-61) and 08.07 `[DEEP]` (:63), and :132 in the same file records 'MoSCoW has since run'. Disk headers confirm the preamble is wrong in both directions: 08.01/08.02/08.04 indexes are [SURFACE], 08.03/08.05 are [BREADTH], 08.05.01/08.05.02/08.05.04/08.07 are [DEEP]. The count sentence also double-counts — disk holds 17 leaf features under the five sub-domains plus 3 domain-level, matching ideation-index.md's '5 sub-domains + 20 features'. Kept at warning rather than blocking: these are pipeline depth markers, not product behaviour, so no implementer invents anything from them.

The load-bearing part of the evidence is false. The finding asserts 08.08-interruption-reconnect-continuity.md:73 is unowned 'unlike its siblings which all name an owner' — but the sibling row at :70 in the same table carries `[Deferred — /create-prd-architecture]` with no owner either, so the row follows the table's own convention, not a deviation from it. The row also carries a live forward target and states that the product behaviour is already settled: 'the behaviour is settled (a threshold declares someone out); the missing part is the number, a threshold with a cost on both sides, same class as `08.05.02` Q-06' — a number routed to /create-prd-compile is the documented mechanism for exactly this class. On the CX half: realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:212 CX-13 states its own answer in the same sentence as the marker ('never writes back — a completed overdub says nothing about playability'), and CX-11 (:208) feeds 08.02.02, which moscow-ledger.md:733 places at WON'T.

All nine markers verified verbatim (08.01-latency-budget-playability-cx.md:36, :55, :59, :74; 08.01.01:56; 08.01.02:62; 08.01.03:56), but every feature they sit in is out of Step 5 scope by an explicit global decision, not by oversight. moscow-ledger.md places 08.01.01 at COULD (:558), 08.01.02 at COULD (:559) and 08.01.03 at WON'T (:732), and ideation-index.md D-24 (:210) states 'Coulds (201) and Won'ts (53) correctly remain `[SURFACE]` — out of Step 5 scope', with :67 ('Could/Won't features at [SURFACE] — 254 — correctly out of Step 5 scope') and :172 ('Could | 201 | `[SURFACE]` — intentionally minimal | deepened at spec time if pursued'). The tree therefore carries a named owner-ratified rule and a named future stage for precisely these markers. 08.03.04:112 shows the convention being applied in-tree: 'Re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5, which per `ideation-index.md` D-24 never covered Coulds.'

Rows verified (08.01-latency-budget-playability-index.md:57 and 08.01.02-playability-verdict-tempo-ceiling.md:104, both 'User | MoSCoW'), but MoSCoW did answer them. moscow-ledger.md:559 places 08.01.02 at COULD on exactly this reasoning — 'it gates rooms that may not ship. If Overdub is the shipping path, the verdict risks being a sophisticated...' — and :558 places 08.01.01 at COULD reasoning identically about routing into Overdub. The answer to 'is the verdict worth building at all' is therefore on record as 'not in the first cut'. What survives is stale bookkeeping — a strikethrough that was applied to the sibling row (08.02 index:58, 'RESOLVED by MoSCoW ... Deferred To: ✅ MoSCoW') and not to these two. No product behaviour is unknown.

Quotes verified (08.01.01-latency-measurement-decomposition.md:67; 08.01-latency-budget-playability-cx.md:24; 08.01.02:59), but what is missing is a number, not a behaviour. All three loci fully specify the user-visible outcome — the ledger dims with an age label and a re-measure prompt, the verdict expires with it, and 'a stale green must never render as green' — leaving only the threshold value, which is an engineering-budget quantity owned by /create-prd-compile. The tree routes this class explicitly: realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:134 Q-05 characterises the residue as 'purely a set of numbers with a cost on both sides of being wrong ... already routed to the performance budget' and re-points it to /create-prd-compile, and 08.06:122 Q-03 does the same for the analogous pre-flight window. The feature is also COULD/[SURFACE] and 'intentionally minimal' per ideation-index.md:172.

Quotes verified (08.02.02-route-aware-radius-correction.md:26, :42-43, :69-70), but this feature is WON'T. moscow-ledger.md:733 places 08.02.02 in § WONT ('Cold-start trap: needs probe history that only substantially exists after real-time r[ooms]'), and ideation-index.md:173 states Won'ts are '`[SURFACE]` — intentionally minimal | retained for traceability, not built'. The sub-domain index records the same conclusion as a resolved question at 08.02-playable-radius-peer-matching-index.md:58 — 'RESOLVED by MoSCoW — the map does not ship early on priors ... the correction loop at WON'T (now)'. A confidence model that nothing will build is not an unresolved product decision; the file's `[PARTIAL]` self-label plus the WON'T placement is the documented mechanism working as designed.

The cited cell disambiguates itself in its own second clause, which the finding quotes and then sets aside. 08.02.03-latency-aware-match-filter.md:22 reads in full: 'Configures whether their room is offered as a real-time-capable endpoint in searches, and against what instrument-pair thresholds. Cannot alter the measured values behind the predicate — only whether they participate.' The trailing sentence forecloses the editable-threshold reading outright, and it agrees with D-02 at :100 ('Domain 08 owns the threshold') and with the sibling guard at 08.02.01:21. No competent implementer reads 'cannot alter the measured values ... only whether they participate' and then builds Operator-editable thresholds. (The finding also renders the clause with bold emphasis that is not present in the file.)

Quotes verified (08.02.02-route-aware-radius-correction.md:51, :60; 08.02-playable-radius-peer-matching-cx.md:36), but they sit in the same WON'T feature as #012 — moscow-ledger.md:733 places 08.02.02 in § WONT, and ideation-index.md:173 designates Won'ts '[SURFACE] — intentionally minimal ... retained for traceability, not built'. Both the notification decision and the materiality threshold belong to a correction loop that the ratified MoSCoW pass decided not to build (08.02 index:58, 'RESOLVED by MoSCoW'). There is no v1 behaviour to invent.

Row verified at 08.02.03-latency-aware-match-filter.md:110, but the ledger answers the question it asks. moscow-ledger.md:561 places 08.02.03 at COULD with the reasoning stated in the question's own terms: 'if the rooms are cut, an "overdub-capable?" predicate replaces it — trivially true for everyone and therefore worthless. Dies with [the rooms]'. So the outcome — the predicate does not survive a rooms cut, and the feature is not in the first cut — is on record. The unstruck 'Deferred To: MoSCoW' cell is stale bookkeeping of the same kind the sibling rows closed properly (08.02 index:58; 08.02.01:101), not an open product decision.

Quotes verified (08.03.04-monitoring-trust-playback-context.md:51-53 vs D-01 at :101 and D-02 at :102), but the answers are in the same file, in its Decisions table, and are restated in its edge cases. :70 repeats D-02 in behavioural form ('Warning is Producer-only. Quotes verified (08.03-remote-monitoring-session-attendance-cx.md:37, :71, :74, :85, :89; 08.03.03:58; 08.03.04:69, :79), but each is covered by a stated rule. The two synthesis blocks name their own mechanism on the line itself — :74 and :89 read 'Medium confidence, deferred per the CX template's rule for non-High entries' — and both CX-03 and CX-04 are pairs whose subject is 08.03.04, which moscow-ledger.md:563 places at COULD and flags 'SPECULATIVE — flagged as such in the file itself', with 08.03.04 Q-01 (:110) still asking whether it is a real product at all. 08.03.03 is likewise COULD (moscow-ledger.md:562), and ideation-index.md D-24 (:210) plus :67/:172 make Coulds explicitly out of Step 5 scope and 'deepened at spec time if pursued'. Quotes verified (08.04-talkback-cue-mixes-cx.md:34; 08.04.01-talkback-channel-ducking.md:56), but duck attack/release times and default depth are DSP performance-budget values, not vision-layer product behaviour — the same class realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:134 routes to /create-prd-compile as 'purely a set of numbers'. Both quotes verified (08.04.02-per-performer-cue-mixes.md:70; 08.08-interruption-reconnect-continuity.md:118 D-05, :62, :87), but they do not actually conflict: 08.04.02:70 states the requirement ('Must survive a reconnect — rebuilding a mix mid-session is a real cost. Interacts with 08.08') and defers only its unstated remainder, while 08.08 D-05 ratifies exactly that requirement in the file that owns reconnect behaviour. Quotes verified (08.04-talkback-cue-mixes-cx.md:61-64, :71), and :71 names its own mechanism verbatim — 'Medium confidence, deferred per the CX template's rule for non-High entries' — which is a stated rule with a stated basis, not an orphan marker. The pair also concerns 08.04.01 and 08.04.03, both placed in § WONT by moscow-ledger.md:734 and :736 and designated 'retained for traceability, not built' by ideation-index.md:173. Moreover the authority question has a governing rule already: 08.04.01 D-03 (:95) 'Performers control talkback's intrusion level but cannot mute it' bounds any carried preference — a minimal-ducking preference cannot become a mute, so the outcome space is already constrained rather than open.

Verified and genuinely contradictory with no marker reconciling the two. 08.05-session-capture-recall-cx.md:83-87 asserts as fact that 'The exact relationship is genuinely unresolved and is the substance of index Q-01', while that index question is struck through and closed at 08.05-session-capture-recall-index.md:64 — '~~Does the attendance record's certainty actually translate into a *credit*?~~ **RESOLVED — it never does.**' — and the specification exists at 08.05.04-session-attendance-provenance.md:77-86, which enumerates the three-component bridge and states 'Presence alone contributes zero ... That is the design, not a gap.' 08.05.04:81 even cites 'parent CX-04' as the source of one component, so the stale CX text is load-bearing in the resolved version. DOWNGRADED to warning: the resolution is explicit and unmissable in both the index and the owning MUST feature, so nothing is invented — the defect is that a CX file still advertises a closed question as open.

Verified as an intra-file contradiction in a MUST/[DEEP] file. 08.05.04-session-attendance-provenance.md:218 still reads 'Works identically under **08.07 Overdub Mode**' and locates the cost solely on the attestation axis ('a solo overdub is `self-attested` end to end'), while the same file's edge row at :166 has been corrected to the grade axis ('The record has delivery-certainty, not performance-certainty ... as `delivered-by`') and its grade row at :50 says the same. The correction target is named explicitly elsewhere — realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:140 and 08.07-overdub-mode.md:333 both declare the 'works identically' wording wrong — so the Cross-Cut Notes bullet is a residual of a remediation that reached the edge row and stopped. Two statements in one file, no marker on either. DOWNGRADED to warning: the corrected semantics are stated three separate times (:50, :166, CX-07), so the divergence is recoverable from the same file rather than forcing invented behaviour.

The Step-6 obligations landed — in the domain CX, which is where cross-sub-domain synthesis belongs per that file's own scoping rule at realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:13 ('internal to a single sub-domain (e.g. 08.05.01↔08.05.02) live in that sub-domain's own CX file'). The witness obligation is carried at CX-03 (:19 and :73: 'per DT-07 the answer decides — at capture time, before the session — whether R2's fallback witness must be enabled'), the pre-flight/alignability obligation at CX-04 (:20 and :89: 'Step 6 added the alignability pre-commitment ... pre-flight must also confirm the session *will be* alignable'), and the talkback constraint on the witness tap at CX-02 (:18, naming 'the pre-talkback timing witness (08.05.02 R2)'). The finding's distinguishing evidence is also false: 08.05-session-capture-recall-cx.md is not 'alone among the six CX files' in lacking a Status/Last-updated header — all five sub-domain CX files (08.01, 08.02, 08.03, 08.04, 08.05) carry only Level and Scope; only the domain CX has the header.
